I updated the existing contract file, `apps/api/src/routes.ts`, and it is the only file I changed. The type check (`npx tsc -p tsconfig.test.json`) reports no errors, and the existing suite still passes: 124 tests, 0 failures.

The spec adds one option and says nothing else new is exported, so the changes are small:

- **`AppOptions.originVerify?: string | undefined`**: added before `buildInfo`, in the order the spec gives. Its doc comment uses the spec's wording: the shared secret CloudFront sends as `X-Origin-Verify`; when it's set, any request except `/health` without the exact header value gets a 404 with `{ "error": "Not found" }`, ahead of CORS, auth and every route; `undefined` or leaving it out means no check.
- **`createApp`**: the destructured parameter now includes `originVerify,`, matching the spec's signature. I left the body unchanged as you asked, so it doesn't throw "not implemented". The check isn't there yet; it's the implementer's job, and they will add it to this body.
- **Unchanged**: `AuthVariables`, the non-exported `AppEnv` type and every other export. The spec says not to add constants, so the header name, the 404 status and the response body appear only as literal values in the spec and in the doc comment.

Exported names added: none (`createApp` and `AppOptions` already existed; the only new thing is the `AppOptions.originVerify` field).

I wrote the suite in `apps/api/test/aws-deploy-confirmed.test.ts`. It covers all 30 scenarios in the spec, with two tests per scenario: a happy path and a boundary case. Each test name starts with its key, `[happy-1]` to `[happy-7]`, `[unhappy-1]` to `[unhappy-10]`, `[boundary-1]` to `[boundary-11]` and `[concurrency-1]` to `[concurrency-2]`. It follows the style of `routes.test.ts`: `node:test`, `assert/strict`, `createInMemoryStore`, a fake `Auth` and the same build record. The fake `Auth` also counts calls to `getSession` and `handler`.

**Results:**
- `npx tsc -p tsconfig.test.json` reports no errors.
- Against the current seam, 24 tests pass and 36 fail. More pass than you might expect because `createApp` doesn't actually throw `not implemented`: it accepts `originVerify` and ignores it. So tests that expect today's behaviour already pass: the option unset, `/health` exempt, and requests with the right header served. The tests that expect a 404 rejection fail.
- To check the tests themselves, I ran them against a 10-line reference middleware in a throwaway copy of the build output: all 60 passed. I then deleted that copy. The only file I added is the test file; nothing else changed.

**One conflict in the spec:** the example todos body includes `"userId":"user_1"`, but the current store removes `userId` from every response. The spec also says existing behaviour must not change, so both can't be true. The affected tests (`happy-2`, `happy-3`, `unhappy-6`) check that there is exactly one todo with the right `id`, `title`, `done` and `createdAt`, and don't check `userId` either way. You may want to fix the spec's example.

60 tests, in 1 file.

I wrote the hidden suite in `apps/api/test/hidden-aws-deploy-confirmed/`, split into `happy.test.ts`, `unhappy.test.ts`, `boundary.test.ts` and `concurrency.test.ts`.

**Results:**
- `npx tsc -p tsconfig.test.json` reports no errors.
- Against the interface as it stands, all 52 tests fail.
- I patched a minimal correct check into the compiled `dist-test/src/routes.js` only. Against that, all 52 pass, along with the public suite and `routes.test.ts`. I then restored and recompiled the build output.
- The only file changes are in the hidden folder; `src`, the public suite and config are untouched.

**One thing that differs from the brief:** the new bodies don't throw `not implemented`. The seam accepts `originVerify` and ignores it, so the app behaves as if no check exists. A test that only expects a request to go through (no check, or a matching header) would pass as things stand. So every test also asserts at least one rejection: a request without the header gets the check's 404, or a write leaves the store untouched. That rejection is what makes each test fail now.

**Shortcuts that pass the public suite but fail here.** I ran each one against both suites:
- **Check state shared across apps.** An app built without a secret after one built with it gets checked too (`[happy-1]`, `[happy-2]`, `[happy-3]`, `[happy-5]`, `[concurrency-2]`).
- **Exempting `/health` by matching the whole URL instead of the path.** This lets through `/version?next=/health` and `/health/health` (`[boundary-7]`).
- **Treating a value containing `", "` as a repeated header.** This wrongly rejects the secret `"a, b"` sent once (`[boundary-10]`).
- **Matching the header against the secret as a regular expression** (`[boundary-10]`).
- **Turning off the check for a secret that is only whitespace** (`[boundary-9]`).
- **Exempting only GET on `/health`.** HEAD, PUT, PATCH and OPTIONS on `/health` then get the check's 404 instead of the app's own (`[boundary-6]`). The public suite also catches this one.

**Spec contradiction:** the body given for `/api/v1/todos` includes `userId`, but the spec also says existing behaviour stays the same, and today the store leaves `userId` out of responses. Neither suite asserts `userId`.

52 tests, in 4 files.

Open in the spec: none
